root_cause.defect: The historical HYPE replay counted every eligible signal received during an open lifecycle as occupied and never compared its side with the open side.
root_cause.live_contract: An executable opposite strategy intent closes the open position without same-cycle reversal.
root_cause.research_effect: The prior replay mislabeled two selected-policy development opposite signals as timer-held lifecycles and therefore understated native-exit economics.

implementation.fill_semantics: decision on completed bar, close at following bar open with configured adverse slippage

validation.tdd_red: Opposite-signal lifecycle test failed because the replay lacked the live-parity configuration and behavior.
validation.tdd_green: Opposite signal now closes next open with reason opposite_strategy_intent and creates no same-cycle reverse entry.

evidence.role: immutable successor replay with exact v51 opposite-intent exit
successor bundle identity and sidecar checksums

limitations: Only two selected-policy development lifecycles exercised the corrected exit and neither later-confirmation lifecycle did.
Development remains fragile: only two of five folds are positive and performance excluding the largest winner remains negative.
Later confirmation contains only four trades and is negative after removing its largest winner.
One-minute OHLC and modeled slippage cannot prove event-level live fills.
The current live HYPE lifecycle remains open; its realized result is not part of this archive comparison.
falsifier: Update this conclusion if exact live opposite signals do not close immediately, if realized execution costs materially exceed the frozen friction contract, if additional compatible lifecycles make native exit negative after largest-winner removal, or if source identity no longer matches the deployed provider.

change_proposal.Recommendation: Retain the current v51 HYPE exit contract and use the corrected opposite-intent-aware replay for all successor HYPE exit comparisons.
change_proposal.Why now: The user required opposite signals to lock profit, and the historical research tool omitted that deployed behavior from development economics.
change_proposal.Evidence reviewed: Live router semantics and tests, prior immutable v4 replay, corrected immutable v5 replay, all selected-policy trade rows, later confirmation, funding, fees, slippage, stop and timer assumptions, and generic profit-lock challengers.
change_proposal.Observed problem or opportunity: Two profitable short lifecycles were incorrectly held to timer exits after executable long signals; correcting them increased selected-policy development net by 380.17 bps.
change_proposal.Applicable market regime: Bidirectional HYPE compression-breakout entries across the frozen development and later-confirmation windows; no regime subset was selected post hoc.
change_proposal.Alternatives considered: Ignore occupied direction, close and reverse in one cycle, close only at timers/stops, add generic profit locks, or model live close-only opposite intent exactly.
change_proposal.Proposed live change: None. Live v51 already closes on opposite executable intent; this change is confined to report-only research replay and its successor evidence identity.
change_proposal.Expected upside: Future exit comparisons use the deployed lifecycle contract, avoid understating profitable opposite closes, and reduce pressure to install historically losing generic profit locks.
change_proposal.Main risks and failure modes: Sparse opposite exits, modeled next-open slippage differing from live fills, outlier dependence, weak fold stability, and accidental use of legacy replay defaults in another command.
change_proposal.Validation completed: Red-green lifecycle regression, no-reversal assertion, frozen command-config regression, 30 focused tests, Ruff, line-limit refactor, immutable replay publication, per-trade reconciliation, and v4-v5 metric comparison.
change_proposal.Validation still required: Resolve the current live HYPE lifecycle and collect additional exact opposite-signal closes with fees, funding, slippage, latency, MFE giveback, and continuous venue protection.
change_proposal.Success metrics: Every opposite executable intent produces one close and zero same-cycle reversal; replay/live exit reasons align; lifecycle accounting reconciles; and native economics remain positive under folds and largest-winner sensitivity.
change_proposal.Failure / rollback triggers: Any missed or duplicate opposite close, same-cycle reversal, stale signal execution, identity mismatch, accounting divergence, or compatible forward evidence that reverses native-exit economics.
change_proposal.Confidence level: High confidence in the diagnosed replay defect and corrected causal mechanics; medium confidence that native exit remains preferable to the three frozen generic locks; low confidence in durable profitability because fold and outlier robustness remain weak.
change_proposal.Explicit approval requested: No live approval requested because deployed v51 behavior is unchanged. The user already approved correcting the report-only parity defect.
